title: Oracles and Deutsch–Jozsa
summary: Constant or balanced with a single query.
mission: With a single call to oracle(qc), leave the input register (qubits 0 to 2) in |000⟩ if the secret function is constant, and with no chance of |000⟩ if it is balanced.

prediction.question: With 3 input bits, how many queries does a deterministic (zero-error) classical algorithm need, in the worst case, to decide whether the function is constant or balanced?
prediction.explanation: If the first 4 queries give the same value, the function can still be balanced; only the fifth decides. In general it takes 2^(n−1) + 1 queries. The quantum algorithm uses one.

hints: Prepare the auxiliary qubit in |−⟩, as in the phase kickback lesson: qc.x(3) and qc.h(3).
Put qubits 0, 1 and 2 in superposition before the oracle and apply Hadamard to them again afterwards.
Sequence: qc.x(3), qc.h(3), Hadamard on qubits 0 to 2, oracle(qc), Hadamard on qubits 0 to 2.
